record.paper_title: (E,E′N) and (E,E′NN) Experiments at NIKHEF, Mainz and JLab and Open Problems in One- and Two-Nucleon Emissions
record.original_question: How does the normal recoil polarization P_N in exclusive (e,e′p) scattering vary with Q², and can that dependence be used to isolate the energy dependence of final-state interactions well enough to clarify nuclear transparency and, ultimately, color transparency? Because P_N vanishes in the absence of final-state interactions, the open problem is to determine whether systematic polarization measurements can cleanly separate genuine attenuation effects from competing reaction-mechanism uncertainties.

evidence.quote: Without FSI, PN = 0. Therefore PN is a good candidate to look at when studying nuclear transparency, as its Q2 dependence reflects the energy dependence of FSI.

As the normal recoil polarization PN vanishes without FSI, its Q2 dependence in exclusive (e,e′p) reactions deserves a detailed study in connection with the problem of nuclear transparency and, ultimately, of color transparency.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider exclusive quasi-elastic electron–nucleus scattering of the form A(e,e'p)B, in which an electron of four-momentum transfer squared Q² knocks a single proton out of a nuclear target while leaving the residual nucleus in a well-defined state. Let n̂ denote the unit vector normal to the scattering plane (the plane spanned by the incident and scattered electron momenta and the ejected proton momentum), and let P_N be the component of the ejected proton's recoil polarization along n̂, induced even with an unpolarized electron beam and an unpolarized target. Under the standard reaction-mechanism description (one-photon exchange, distorted-wave impulse approximation with final-state interactions modeled by an optical potential or Glauber-type rescattering), P_N is generated entirely by final-state interactions (FSI) between the outgoing proton and the residual nuclear system: in the absence of FSI one has P_N = 0.

(a) Determine the dependence of P_N on Q² for representative target nuclei (e.g., ¹²C, ¹⁶O, ⁴⁰Ca) in the kinematic regime accessible at modern electron-scattering facilities (Q² up to several GeV²), as a function of missing momentum and outgoing-proton kinematics.

(b) Decide whether the measured Q²-dependence of P_N can be used to isolate the energy dependence of FSI cleanly enough to (i) extract a model-independent nuclear transparency, and (ii) provide an unambiguous signal of color transparency — i.e., the predicted onset, at sufficiently large Q², of a suppression of FSI due to the propagation of a small-size, color-neutral configuration of the struck proton through the nuclear medium — while disentangling such effects from competing reaction-mechanism uncertainties (relativistic effects, two-body currents, spinor distortion, off-shell ambiguities, choice of optical potential).
artifact.category_tag: nuclear electron scattering and color transparency
artifact.status_search_result: The Q²-dependence of the induced normal recoil polarization P_N in (e,e'p) reactions remains an active probe of FSI and color transparency. Recent theoretical and experimental work (including JLab 12 GeV proposals and 2022–2024 analyses on D(e,e'p)n and related processes) continues to discuss P_N as a candidate observable, but no clean, model-independent extraction of color transparency from P_N has been established; signals at intermediate Q² remain inconclusive and entangled with conventional reaction-mechanism effects.

status_evidence.title: Searching for an Enhanced Signal of the Onset of Color Transparency in Baryons with D(e,e′p)n Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses polarization and Q² dependence in (e,e'p) as probes of FSI and color transparency, noting that polarization observables vanish in the color-transparency limit and are sensitive to FSI.
status_evidence.claim: Polarization observables in (e,e'p) are still being proposed as sensitive probes of the onset of color transparency, indicating the problem remains under active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Executive Summary (Electron-Nucleus scattering white paper)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews open questions in nuclear transparency and color transparency, including the use of recoil polarization observables.
status_evidence.claim: Recent community white papers list extraction of color transparency from (e,e'p) observables as an unresolved problem.

status_evidence.title: Color coherence effects in the reaction 2H(p,2p)n
status_evidence.snippet: 2023 study on color-coherence and FSI effects in hard nuclear reactions.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study FSI/color-transparency signatures, supporting the status of the question as open.
